To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the effectiveness of CLVR is affected by the source of the query expansion (QE), (2) the effectiveness of the QE is affected by the field of metadata, (3) the most robust source of metadata for QE is the title of the video, (4) the most robust fields of metadata for QE are the title, description and keywords, and (5) the least robust field of metadata for QE in the context of CLVR is the transcript.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing and evaluating new techniques that can improve CLIR effectiveness for user created video content, which is an important and challenging task for multimedia information retrieval.
the development of novel techniques that can improve the effectiveness of CLIR in the context of UGC content.
the development of novel techniques to improve CLVR of UGC content.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our work proposes a novel technique that improves the effectiveness of CLIR for UGC content by adaptively selecting the most reliable metadata field and the most suitable QE technique for that field.
this work has shown the potential of metadata fields and query expansion in improving CLIR effectiveness of UGC content.
this work shows how the use of different sources of metadata and the use of query expansion can be effective in improving CLIR effectiveness of user generated internet video.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a novel adaptive QE method for CLVR of noisy UGC content that is able to predict the most reliable source of metadata for expansion, which can improve the retrieval effectiveness by 15% absolute in terms of mean average precision.

we show how different metadata fields can be utilised for CLIR and that the use of query expansion can have a positive or negative impact on CLIR effectiveness, depending on the source of the expansion.
our proposed techniques for improving CLIR of UGC content are able to achieve a 20% improvement over a baseline system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CLVR task is significantly different from CLIR and CLVR tasks for formal content.
different sources of information have varying robustness to QE and that an adaptive QE technique that can predict the most reliable source can be effective for CLIR of UGC content.

the use of metadata fields for query expansion can be beneficial in the CLVR context, but the effectiveness of each field can be highly variable, and hence the choice of field for query expansion should be adaptive.
